invariant: json.decode(text) is available in every tier with no capability grant, reuses the same trusted in-guest JSON decoder net.fetch_json uses (never a second decoder), and applies the identical depth/node/size budget net.fetch_json applies to a fetched response, checked before the text is ever decoded.

cases: well-formed object/array/scalar/null text under a read-only trigger with no capabilities configured
text past the shared byte-size cap
text whose parsed shape exceeds the shared depth cap
text whose parsed shape exceeds the shared node-count cap
a null array element versus a null object value, matching net.fetch_json's own decode semantics

mustHold: json.decode is reachable and callable under a read-only trigger with zero grants
a well-formed input decodes to a genuine guest-native value, not a live host-object handle
malformed text fails cleanly and is catchable by the guest, never a crash or hang
a non-string argument is rejected before any parsing is attempted
an over-budget input (by size, depth, or node count) is rejected before the full decode runs, with the same reason taxonomy a return-value marshal rejection uses
the depth/node/size numbers enforced here are the SAME numbers net.fetch_json enforces on a fetched body, not independently tuned
